whatChanged.categoryZh: 人工智能 / 网络安全
whatChanged.headline: OpenAI's New Cybersecurity AI Can Find Exploits. Who Gets to Use It?
whatChanged.headlineZh: OpenAI 新模型能找出可利用的漏洞，谁可以使用？
intro: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November, a specialist model that can investigate software vulnerabilities and develop working exploits. That ability is useful to defenders who need to test and fix weaknesses, but it could also help attackers.

OpenAI rates the model "Critical" for cybersecurity under its own Preparedness Framework. For now, access is restricted to selected, approved Daybreak Red customers rather than everyone using ChatGPT.
introZh: 2026 年 11 月 5 日，OpenAI 发布专门研究网络安全的 GPT-6 Cyber。它可以分析软件漏洞，并尝试开发真正能利用这些漏洞的攻击程序。安全团队可以借此验证问题、修复系统，但同样的能力也可能被攻击者滥用。
OpenAI 按自己的安全评估框架，将它的网络安全能力评为“Critical”（关键级）。目前仅向经过批准的部分 Daybreak Red 客户开放，并非普通 ChatGPT 用户都能使用。

sections.heading: What can the model actually do?
paragraphs: On OpenAI's ExploitGym benchmark, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%, versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber. The test measures whether a model can exploit specified vulnerabilities in controlled targets; it does not measure success against arbitrary websites.

OpenAI also says its researchers used the model to identify 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and develop 948 privilege-escalation exploits targeting Linux. Mozilla has already released fixes for many of the reported Firefox issues, according to OpenAI. These are company-reported research results, not proof that the model can reliably break into any system.
paragraphsZh: 在 OpenAI 的 ExploitGym 测试中，GPT-6 Cyber 得分为 48.5%，上一代 GPT-5.6 Cyber 为 32.1%。测试考察的是模型能否在受控环境中利用指定漏洞，并不意味着它可以随意攻破真实网站。
OpenAI 还称，研究人员借助该模型发现了 Firefox 中 81 个此前未知的高危漏洞，并开发出 948 个针对 Linux 的提权漏洞利用程序。该公司表示，Mozilla 已发布其中许多 Firefox 漏洞的修复程序。这些是公司公布的研究成果，不能推导出模型对任何系统都能成功入侵。

sections.heading: Can it respect the limits of an authorized test?
paragraphs: Security researchers often have permission to test one system but not its neighbors. In an OpenAI evaluation with deliberately tempting out-of-scope services, the new model avoided exploiting those services in 99.93% of cases without a deployment safety prompt, compared with 94.49% for the previous model. With the deployment prompt, OpenAI reports 100% in that specific evaluation.

These figures are encouraging but narrow. Passing a designed test does not guarantee perfect behavior in the real world. OpenAI says it combines model training with monitoring, network restrictions and oversight.
paragraphsZh: 网络安全测试通常有明确授权范围。研究人员可以测试某台服务器，却未必有权触碰旁边的系统。
OpenAI 设置了一项测试：让模型在完成任务时遇到容易攻击、但不属于授权范围的其他服务。在没有部署安全提示的条件下，新模型有 99.93% 的测试没有越界，上一代为 94.49%。加上部署提示后，OpenAI 报告该测试中没有越界案例。但单项测试达到 100%，不代表现实中绝对不会出错。公司还采用监测、网络访问限制和人工监督等措施。

sections.heading: Why restrict access?
sections.headingZh: 为什么不向所有人开放？
paragraphs: The same ability to find a flaw can help a company patch it or help someone exploit it. OpenAI is initially offering GPT-6 Cyber through API and Codex to selected Daybreak Red customers approved for advanced security testing. It says broader access to approved customers will follow. No general-public release date was announced in the launch post.
paragraphsZh: 找出漏洞的技术既能帮助修补系统，也可能帮助实施攻击。GPT-6 Cyber 首先通过 API 和 Codex 向部分获批的 Daybreak Red 客户开放，主要面向授权的高级安全研究。OpenAI 表示会逐步扩大获批客户范围，但发布公告没有给出面向所有普通用户的开放日期。

whatChanged.ending: The difficult part is no longer just building AI that finds security flaws. It is deciding who may use that ability, on which systems, and under whose supervision.
whatChanged.endingZh: 现在的问题不只是 AI 能发现多少漏洞，还包括谁能使用这种能力、可以测试哪些系统，以及由谁监督。

stayCurious.categoryZh: 新加坡 / 自然 / 日常生活
stayCurious.headline: Why Do Singapore's Rain Trees Fold Their Leaves Before Sunset?
stayCurious.headlineZh: 新加坡的雨树为什么天还没黑就开始合拢叶子？
intro: Look closely at one of Singapore's enormous roadside rain trees in the late afternoon. Its tiny leaflets may already be folding together, even though it is still light outside.
The rain tree has another local name, Pukul Lima, or "five o'clock" in Malay. That name preserves an intriguing clue about both the tree and Singapore's old clock.
introZh: 傍晚走在新加坡街头，如果仔细看路边的大雨树，会发现那些小叶片在天还亮着时就开始合拢了。
雨树还有个马来语名字 Pukul Lima，意思是“五点钟”。这个名字不仅和树的习性有关，还藏着一段新加坡时间制度的历史。

sections.heading: Is the tree responding to rain or the time of day?
paragraphs: NParks says the leaflets fold in the evening and also during overcast weather. Its heritage-tree records describe them beginning to close about an hour and a half before sunset and reopening after sunrise. This folding behavior is one explanation for the English name "rain tree." NParks also notes another possible origin: droplets of secretions from sap-sucking cicadas on the tree.
It is not a dependable rain forecast. A folded leaf tells you about the plant's response to conditions, not that a shower is certain.
paragraphsZh: 国家公园局 NParks 介绍，雨树的小叶片在傍晚会合拢，阴天也可能如此。其古树档案记载，叶片通常在日落前约一个半小时开始闭合，日出后再逐渐展开。
这种阴天合叶的习性，是“雨树”名称的一种解释；NParks 也提到，树上蝉类等吸汁昆虫的分泌物形成的“雨滴”，可能是名称的另一来源。但它并不是可靠的天气预报器。叶子合拢，不代表一定会下雨。

sections.heading: Why is it called "five o'clock"?
paragraphs: NParks explains that 5 pm was once closer to sunset in Singapore and Malaysia, before standard-time changes on 1 January 1982. The Malay nickname Pukul Lima reflects the old relationship between the clock and evening light. The tree has not changed its habits just because the official clock changed.
paragraphsZh: NParks 指出，1982 年 1 月 1 日新加坡与马来西亚调整标准时间之前，下午五点曾更接近日落时刻。因此人们用 Pukul Lima 来称呼这种傍晚收拢叶片的树。后来钟表上的时间变了，树依然按光照等环境条件活动。

sections.heading: Has this tree always grown here?
sections.headingZh: 它是新加坡原生树种吗？
paragraphs: No. The rain tree, Samanea saman, comes from tropical America. NParks records that it was introduced to Singapore in 1876. Its broad, umbrella-shaped crown can spread roughly 20 to 30 metres, making it a popular shade tree along roads and in open spaces. Mature branches can also host ferns and orchids.
Next time you pass a rain tree at dusk, look up. Its leaves may already be preparing for the night.
paragraphsZh: 不是。雨树学名 Samanea saman，原产热带美洲，1876 年引入新加坡。它的树冠像一把巨大的伞，宽度可达约 20 至 30 米，因此长期被用作行道树和遮阴树。老树的枝干上还常能看到蕨类和兰花附生。
下次傍晚走过雨树，不妨抬头看看。它可能已经开始“睡觉”了。

stayCurious.ending: A familiar roadside tree can tell you something about changing light, weather and even the history of local time.
stayCurious.endingZh: 一棵熟悉的行道树，原来也能让人看见光线、天气和本地时间的变化。
